name: Gravel
manufacturer: Various the Gray Zone cooks, commonly attributed to a distributor called 'Mamo' in the Chicago South the Gray Zone
description: A crude amphetamine analogue cooked from stolen hospital ephedrine stock, battery acid neutralized with baking soda, and industrial degreaser. The name comes from the visible particulate matter suspended in the product — it never fully dissolves. Delivers a hard, jittery stimulant rush that keeps the Gray Zone workers functional through brutal double shifts.
effects: suppressed hunger and fatigue for 6-10 hours
side_effects: vein scarring and collapse at injection sites
particulate matter causes micro-embolisms over time
cultural_context: Gravel is the fuel of the Gray Zone economy. Dock workers, scrap haulers, and night-shift assemblers use it to push through work that would otherwise be physically impossible. There's no shame in it at Tier 1 — it's survival. Long-term users develop a distinctive hand tremor called 'the gravel shake' that marks them visually. Tier 2 workers look down on it; the Gray Zone residents look at it as a necessary evil.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone community is losing workers to mass cardiac events — someone cut this batch of Gravel with an industrial coagulant, and nobody knows if it was accident or sabotage
A Tier 3 journalist wants to embed with Gravel users to expose labor conditions, but she quickly realizes the story is more complicated than she expected
The cook known as Mamo has gone missing, and three different the Gray Zone factions are tearing the district apart looking for her recipe
